clue.text: I'm a girl — you'll see me around wearing beads

indicators.note: the beads are worn by the reversed word, which sits inside them like a body in clothes

parts.note: a rosary is a string of prayer beads

indicators.note: turned around, the little word me is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl introduces herself as the one seen wearing a necklace of beads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like the container signal, but it is the reversal; 'wearing' is what puts one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a female first name, so it is a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Deduction from the Commodore's ignoble surrender

indicators.note: a deduction is something taken away, so letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A naval commodore's shameful capitulation is deplored.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a post or concede defeat in chess is to throw in the towel, a kind of surrender.

clue.text: Hedge, a form of barrier

definitions.meaning: to hedge is to stall evasively, as a batsman or politician does when blocking
a wall built of stone is a kind of barrier

explanation.definitionFit: Stalling evasively is a verb sense of the word; a masonry wall is the literal sense, both distinct from a hedge of shrubs.

clue.text: Arab lad seen with difficulty in the gloom

indicators.note: the jumbled lad is placed inside the word for gloom

parts.note: murk is darkness or gloom

indicators.note: something seen with difficulty is blurred and confused, so the letters of lad are muddled

explanation.surface: A young Arab boy can barely be made out in the darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' here is the old phrase 'street arab', a homeless child; 'seen with difficulty' is an unusual anagram signal, picturing a blurred shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudlark was a Victorian street urchin scavenging on riverbanks, and 'street arab' is an old term for such a child.

clue.text: This you can fire or sack

definitions.meaning: a firearm with a grooved barrel is something you discharge
to sack is to plunder or ransack

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a long gun that is discharged; the verb means to search and plunder, matching sack in its looting sense.

clue.text: Slow, to deliver without a little money

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the delivering phrase sits around the money

parts.note: to deliver someone from something is to rid them of it
P is a penny, a small amount of British money

explanation.surface: A sluggish courier is criticised for delivering without any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: P sits inside TORID.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means sluggish and inactive, as a hibernating animal is.

clue.text: Creature presenting heartless mates with a problem

indicators.note: losing the heart means one of the central letters of the word for mates is removed

parts.note: oppos is British slang for friends or mates, from opposite numbers
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone presents unfeeling friends with a puzzle to solve.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPOS, British forces slang for mates, loses a middle P, leaving OPOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a tree-dwelling American marsupial, a creature.

clue.text: Kind of bear quietly leaving tree

indicators.note: the soft-music letter departs from the tree's name

parts.note: a poplar is a tall tree
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A bear slips silently away from a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The white Arctic bear is one species of bear, named for the regions around the poles.

clue.text: Hand out girl's money to speakers

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, with the possessive S

indicators.note: the coins' name is as heard by those speaking it, so the spelling changes

parts.note: pence are British coins, money

explanation.surface: Someone distributes a girl's pocket money to people giving speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to distribute or give out, as a pharmacist does with medicine.

clue.text: Fancy mother's about ready to move

indicators.note: the mother word goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother; the 's is 'has'

indicators.note: letters made to move change their positions, so ready is rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother is almost ready to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' turns READY into AYDRE, which DAM goes about.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy can be an idle fantasy or reverie, as a waking dream is.

clue.text: Impending disaster — doom draws close, following explosion…

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters fly into a new order

parts.note: f is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: With catastrophe looming, doom closes in after a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: DOOM DRAWS CLOSE plus F are blown apart and rebuilt into the three-word phrase; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Damocles sat under a blade hung by a single hair, so the phrase means a threat hanging over someone.

clue.text: …produced by this foreigner, in work but retired

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the assembled word is read backwards
the foreigner is placed inside the unit of work

parts.note: the erg is a scientific unit of work
a Dane, a native of Denmark, is a foreigner to a British setter

explanation.surface: An explosion is caused by a foreigner who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from 10, so the explosion there is what is 'produced by this'. 'retired' turns the whole container round.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown bomb is the thing that causes a blast, linking back to the explosion in the previous clue.

clue.text: Be entitled to reassemble severed parts

indicators.note: to reassemble is to put pieces back together in a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon claims the right to reattach parts that have been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' just completes the picture of the cut-off pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to have earned a right to it.

clue.text: A sporting event to fire the nation

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
a race can mean a people or nation

explanation.surface: A sports contest that will inspire the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: A sack race is a children's sports-day event where runners hop inside sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The hopping contest in sacks is a fun competition at school sports days.

clue.text: Snail, say, suffers breakdown

indicators.note: something that suffers is damaged and knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snail, for instance, has a collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown of figures is a detailed examination of its parts.

clue.text: Scholars take in most of the science

indicators.note: the scholars enclose what follows, holding it inside

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree, scholars

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Academics absorb the bulk of the scientific subject.
explanation.walkthrough: MA is the Master of Arts degree, so scholars are MAs in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The British short name for mathematics, a science of numbers.

clue.text: One getting this will have spare capital

definitions.text: One getting this will have spare capital

parts.words: One getting this will have spare capital
parts.note: capital is read as the head and spare as thin, so the person has sparse hair up top, not money in hand

explanation.definitionFit: A balding person has sparse hair on the crown of the head.

clue.text: Chews up child in the last act

indicators.note: the child is put inside the turned-round word
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: gnaws means chews
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Someone eats a child during the final scene of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only works because this is a down entry, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan was fabled to sing just before dying, so the phrase means a final performance.

clue.text: City depicted by novelist

definitions.meaning: a small cathedral city in Somerset, England
H. G. ..., the English author of The War of the Worlds

explanation.definitionFit: England's smallest cathedral city shares its name with the science fiction writer H. G.

clue.text: Part of gang surrounding FBI agents

indicators.note: the gang word goes around the agents, enclosing them

parts.note: a set is a group or gang of people
G-men are US federal agents, government men

explanation.surface: A section of a criminal gang encircles some FBI officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a portion or piece of a whole, like a slice of orange.

clue.text: Theoretical resting place

definitions.meaning: an ... critic or general has opinions without practical experience
a comfortable chair with arms for relaxing in

explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the seat describes someone with only theoretical knowledge; as a noun it is a padded seat to relax in.

clue.text: Dunce has term at school understanding needed

parts.note: at some British public schools a term is called a half
wit is intelligence or understanding

explanation.surface: A slow pupil needs to understand things during the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton and some other English private schools call each term a 'half'.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a foolish or slow person, like a dunce.

clue.text: Game's first rule written up by carpenter's mate

indicators.note: the turned-round rule is placed first, ahead of the game
in a down clue, written up means the letters run from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a law is a rule
RU is rugby union, the game, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: The first rule of a game is recorded by a woodworker's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Game's first' as 'the game has first', putting the turned rule ahead. The Walrus and the Carpenter is a poem in Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's poem the walrus is the carpenter's companion as they eat the oysters.

clue.text: Flowers about in those times

indicators.note: turned about, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the times word is put inside the archaic word for those

parts.note: yon is an old word for that or those
ages are long times or eras

explanation.surface: Flowers were all around back in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole container round, not just one piece; 'yon' is an archaic word for those.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy or bunch of fragrant blooms.

clue.text: Start working with a brush.

definitions.meaning: a brush is a brief skirmish

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means get going on a job; the noun means a short fight or skirmish.

clue.text: Ring a number back and get a very militant woman

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell

indicators.note: back means the following letters are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: Phone a number back and reach a highly aggressive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellona was the Roman goddess of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellona is the Roman war goddess, so a figure for a warlike woman.

clue.text: Man, one about to leave church

indicators.note: the pieces depart from the church word, being taken out of it

parts.note: a basilica is a type of church
I is the Roman numeral for one
ca is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A single man is about to walk out of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a male first name, so a man.

clue.text: Superb trees, fit for what is devised

indicators.note: something devised is invented anew, so these letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Trees suited to whatever has been planned.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from grading diamonds, the finest stones being of the first water.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means of the highest quality, from the clearest grade of diamonds.

clue.text: King and Emperor met in a cave

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors

explanation.surface: Two monarchs held a summit inside a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: GR appears on British postboxes as the cipher of a King George.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave.

clue.text: Amphibious animal — a tailless variety with extra covering

indicators.note: the extra word wraps over what follows, holding it inside

parts.note: plus means extra or in addition

indicators.note: without a tail, the last letter goes

parts.note: a type is a sort or variety

explanation.surface: An animal at home in water and on land is a breed lacking a tail with an extra coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks like a word for the platy fish, but it is the type in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed Australian mammal lives both in rivers and on land.
